**Finding re-submitted: compliant** (no redline, no counterparty comment).

The repair addressed the failed presence check without changing the substantive conclusion, which the verifier confirmed on both material terms:

- **Quote tightened** to the operative customer-right language — "Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement" — so the Customer convenience right is visible on the face of the finding rather than buried inside TrueLink's service-continuation obligation.
- **Rationale now states the right explicitly**: §14 lets Client terminate at will on written notice, with no cause, consent, breach precondition, or exit charge; effective notice ~30–60 days, inside the preferred 30-day window.
- **Root cause recorded**: the right is drafted obliquely (as TrueLink's duty to keep serving until Client's elected termination date) rather than as an express "Client may terminate for convenience" grant. That is a drafting-style artifact, not a substantive gap, so it does not warrant a redline.

Unchanged: TrueLink has no mid-term convenience exit (§13's only unilateral cut-off is cause-based), the 12-month term defeats the multi-year walk-away, and the two shortfalls — no express pro-rata refund (moot under §5a's monthly arrears billing) and the mutual 30-day non-renewal notice — stay noted rather than flagged, the latter because tightening it would cut against our own flexibility.

The one item I would still close out commercially: §14 is expressed as "Subject to Section 4 hereof," and Section 4 was not in the reviewed text. §6 (p0047) indicates Section 4 covers minimum monthly fees, so I have surfaced this as a confirmation item rather than a breach — but if Section 4 turns out to condition or restrict Client's termination right (for example by preserving minimum monthly fees post-termination), this rule should be reopened, since that would function as an early-termination charge.
